---
title: The commands
description: Each command of smalldocs, with its options.
order: 9
---

Each command takes the folder of the project, which holds `_smalldocs.yml` or `_quarto.yml`. If you give no folder, the
command uses the folder you are in.

## render

```bash
smalldocs render [DIR] [--quiet] [--strict]
```

`render` builds the site. With `--quiet`, it prints only warnings and errors. With `--strict`, a
warning makes the exit code 1. A broken link and an option that smalldocs ignores are warnings.

## preview

```bash
smalldocs preview [DIR] [--port 4200] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--no-browser]
```

`preview` builds the site, serves it and opens a browser. When a file of the project changes, it
builds the site again, and the browser loads the new pages. If a build fails, the command prints the
error and keeps the last good site. It listens on this computer only. To listen on other addresses, give `--host`.

## check

```bash
smalldocs check [DIR]
```

`check` builds the site into a temporary folder, and keeps your output folder as it is. It still
writes the API pages and runs the `pre-render` and `post-render` commands, as a build does. Then it
lists what to fix:

- the options that smalldocs ignores
- the broken links
- the Markdown that smalldocs does not read or does not run, with the file and the line of each. Examples
  are citations, cross-references, grid tables and code cells

If it finds anything, the exit code is 1.

## api

```bash
smalldocs api build|check|list [--dir DIR]
smalldocs api check --shown [--dir DIR]
smalldocs api module NAME [--dir DIR]
```

`api` makes the reference pages, checks the docments, lists the documented names, or prints one module as
Markdown. With `--shown`, `check` looks only at what the pages show, and leaves out private names and
names outside `__all__`. See [The API reference](api.qmd).

## publish

```bash
smalldocs publish gh-pages [DIR] [--branch gh-pages] [--remote origin] [--no-render] [-m MESSAGE]
```

`publish` builds the site and pushes it to the branch. It works in a temporary worktree, so your
files and your current branch do not change. Your git hooks do not run for the commit of the site.

It refuses some branches, because they hold your source files:

- your current branch
- the default branch of the remote
- `main` and `master`
- a branch that shares history with your code and holds no site

With `--no-render`, the command publishes the output folder as it is.

## add

```bash
smalldocs add SOURCE [--dir DIR] [--force]
```

`add` copies the theme extensions of a git repository into the folder `_extensions/` of the
project. SOURCE is `org/repo` on GitHub, `org/repo@ref`, a git URL, a local git repository, or a local
folder. It clones `org/repo` over ssh, so a private repository works with your own key. If an extension
is already there, the command asks before it replaces the extension. `--force` replaces it without a
question. See [Themes](themes.qmd).

## themes

```bash
smalldocs themes [DIR]
```

`themes` lists the bundled themes, and the extensions in `_extensions/` with the source of each.

## notebooks lint

```bash
smalldocs notebooks lint [DIR]
```

`notebooks lint` lists the packages that each notebook imports. It checks them against the disallow
list, a list of packages that do not run in Pyodide, the Python that runs in the browser. A notebook
also fails lint when its kernel is not Python, or when it has no code cells. The command runs no
notebook code and needs no JupyterLite installation. It exits with code 1 if a notebook fails lint.
See [Run notebooks in the browser](browser-notebooks.qmd).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Done, with something to fix: `--strict` with warnings, `check` and `api check` with findings, or `notebooks lint` with a notebook that fails |
| 2 | Stopped: no `_smalldocs.yml` or `_quarto.yml`, a bad option, a failed script, a port in use, or a failed clone |
